subject: Workplace Skills
title: The Promotion Document
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Promotion Document.

hook.text: A Google engineer wrote a self-promotion document. It made the case for her promotion so clearly her manager used it verbatim.

buildup.text: Managers juggle many reports. If you don't document your achievements, they'll forget half of them during reviews.

discovery.text: Keep a running document of wins: problems solved, impact delivered, scope expanded. Add entries monthly.

twist.text: Frame achievements as impact, not activity. 'Reduced churn by 15%' beats 'built a retention dashboard.'

climax.text: Before review season, condense your wins into a one-page case. Map each win to the criteria for the next level.

punchline.text: Write your case in impact. Hand it to your manager.

quiz.question: How should achievements be framed in a promotion document?
options: List every task you completed during the review period
Frame achievements as measurable impact, not activity
Focus on the hours worked and effort invested
